issues.body: The new comment says `Quad_Subject` and `Quad_Object` both include `Quad`, and the feature block tests `factory.quad(..., innerQuad)` as an object. In the current RDF/JS Data Model specification, `subject` includes `Quad`, but `object` is listed as NamedNode, Literal, BlankNode, or Variable; it does not include Quad. The feature probe also requires object-position support, so an implementation that correctly supports the specified subject-position quoted Quad but rejects Quad objects will have the entire quoted-triple block skipped, including valid subject-position checks. Conversely, an implementation accepting Quad objects is being tested against an extension rather than the cited conformance contract.
issues.fix_hint: Align the suite with the normative RDF/JS contract: detect quoted triples using a Quad in subject position only, remove or explicitly separate the object-position assertion as a clearly named non-conformance extension, and ensure the subject-position, recursive-equality, and copy tests still run for implementations supporting the specified Quad-subject capability.
issues.title: Quoted Quad objects are not part of the cited RDF/JS Quad object domain

issues.body: The new README text advertises “a `Quad` in the subject/object position” as RDF/JS conformance coverage, but the cited RDF/JS Data Model specification currently includes `Quad` only in the subject domain. This makes the documented scope inaccurate.
issues.fix_hint: Document the normative subject-position coverage. If object-position support is retained as an optional extension test, label it explicitly as such and keep its detection independent from the normative quoted-subject tests.
issues.title: README overstates quoted triples as valid in both subject and object positions

verdict.summary: The directional-literal coverage and recursive keying are coherent, but the quoted-triple block asserts an object-position capability that the cited RDF/JS Data Model specification does not define. That makes the proposed conformance suite capable of rejecting an implementation for behavior outside the specification it claims to test.
